Maximum spring flow in the project area from the Rosebud-McKay and Robinson coal beds is between 0.5 and 5 gpm (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 1). Based on information provided by land owners, it is estimated that 90 percent of the total ground-water consumption in the Project Area and surrounding vicinity is for supplying livestock. Most of the domestic and stock wells in the area are completed in the sub-Robinson unit at depths of 50 to 300 feet (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 1). Westmoreland Resources plans to use 90,000 to 250,000 gallons per day for road sprinkling and fire protection and 10,000 gallons per day for household and sanitary purposes. Sprinkling of roads to control dust will be done in the dryer part of the year and will consume most of the water used. The actual amount needed to control dust will depend on the degree of development and the length of the haulage roads. The present source of this water is a well drilled to the Madison formation.
Sub-irrigation - Sub-irrigated lands are considered as those lands which are cultivated and use shallow ground water to supply the water needs of the crops. Sub-irrigation means that roots of crop plants reach the ground-water table, generally considered to be within 5 to 10 feet of ground surface. The extent to which sub-irrigation is occurring in the Project Area is presently unknown but is thought to be quite limited based on review and analysis of existing information. Ground-water levels in the alluvial wells in the Project Area show the permanent water table well below root zones of locally grown crops, except perhaps alfalfa.
